title: Conway's 99-graph, srg(99, 14, 1, 2)
statement: Find a graph on 99 vertices, 14-regular, in which every two adjacent vertices have exactly one common neighbour and every two non-adjacent vertices exactly two: a strongly regular graph srg(99, 14, 1, 2). J. H. Conway offered $1,000 for deciding whether it exists. A valid graph scores 1.
submission: Text file: the graph in graph6 or sparse6 (as on House of Graphs), as an edge list (one edge "u v" per line, vertices numbered from 0) or as a 0/1 adjacency matrix.
score: 1 for a valid graph; none is known, so the best known value is 0

best_known.source: existence unknown: A. E. Brouwer's table of strongly regular graphs on 51-100 vertices marks (99, 14, 1, 2) with '?'; read 9 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: A. E. Brouwer, Parameters of strongly regular graphs
